宅.meaning: Under a low <part>roof</part>, one bent wire <part>hanger</part> hangs on a nail by the door, holding your coat and scarf. Wherever that hanger hangs, you kick off your shoes and sigh. That's <kanji>home</kanji>.
宅.on: Your first night there, you eat a crunchy <sound>ta</sound>co on the sofa and drop beans all over the new rug.

突.meaning: A <part>large</part> man crouches below a dark <part>hole</part> in the cave roof, then shoots straight up through it with his spear held high, poking at the bats hanging inside. Jab! Jab! He's out to <kanji>stab</kanji> anything up there.
突.on: He jabs so hard that a <sound>to</sound>tem pole beside him topples into the sea and sets off a little <sound>tsu</sound>nami.
突.kun: A bat jabbed in the bottom squeaks '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' and flaps off into the dark.

列.meaning: A pirate lines up old <part>bones</part> along the deck, skull, rib, shin, and taps each one with his <part>dagger</part> to count them. Not one is allowed out of place: they stand in a neat <kanji>row</kanji>.
列.on: Down the row he pours little glasses of <sound>rets</sound>ina, one for every bone.

私.meaning: A farmer hugs one stalk of <part>grain</part> to his chest, his <part>elbow</part> crooked round it so nobody else can reach. 'Mine. Keep off.' It isn't for sharing: it's <kanji>private</kanji>.
私.on: He props a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld in front of it with a sign: Keep Out.
私.kun: A crow swoops. '<sound>Wah</sound>!' the farmer yells, swatting it with a <sound>ta</sound>co while his <sound>shee</sound>p bleats: 'Hands off, that's mine!'

毛.meaning: Three short hairs stand in a stack on a curly tail that swishes off to the right. Stroke it the wrong way and it bristles. It's soft, it sheds all over your sofa, and it's all <kanji>fur</kanji>.
毛.on: The dog sheds so much that you have to cut the carpet with a lawn <sound>mow</sound>er.
毛.kun: A clump of fur floats down and lands right in your <sound>ke</sound>tchup.

費.meaning: At the beach café, every <part>shellfish</part> on the menu has a <part>dollar sign</part> stamped on its shell, and the more you eat, the more signs pile up. One oyster, two oysters, ten. The bill is a huge <kanji>expense</kanji>.
費.on: You pay, stand up to leave, and a <sound>hee</sound>l snaps off the fancy new shoes you bought to look rich.
費.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' you sneeze at the bill, and '<sound>Ee</sound>!' you squeak at the total you spent.

煙.meaning: A <part>fire</part> crackles on a mound of <part>soil</part>, and a wind from the <part>west</part> pushes its grey clouds straight into your face. You cough, your eyes water, and you can't see a thing for the <kanji>smoke</kanji>.
煙.on: An old steam <sound>en</sound>gine chugs past, puffing even more of it into the air.
煙.kun: A cow staggers out of the haze with soot on its nose, knocks over a <sound>ke</sound>ttle and gives one short, choked '<sound>Mu</sound>!'

喫.meaning: You make a <part>pledge</part> to finish everything on the table, and your <part>mouth</part> gets to work: soup, cake, a whole pot of tea, the lot. Not a crumb is left. You <kanji>consume</kanji> it all.
喫.on: A <sound>kit</sound>ten sneaks onto the table and licks the last plate clean.
喫.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' squeaks the kitten, as you gulp down the last drop of tea.

果.meaning: An old <part>tree</part> wears a whole <part>rice field</part> balanced in its branches, square and green. When you shake the trunk, round red apples tumble out of the paddies. It's the tree's best <kanji>fruit</kanji>.
果.on: One apple lands in the pond, and a big <sound>ca</sound>rp swallows it whole.
果.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' cries the farmer, catching the last apple in his hat: the harvest is carried out.

効.meaning: At a crowded party, the guests <part>mingle</part> and sip a strange green drink. One by one their arms bulge with <part>muscle</part>, and soon they're lifting the sofa for fun. Whatever was in that drink, it had an <kanji>effect</kanji>.
効.on: Even the waiter's ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne grows little arms and flexes.
効.kun: It works on everything: one sip and you can bend a brass <sound>key</sound> with your little finger.

常.meaning: Every morning, Grandpa hangs the same striped <part>towel</part> on the same hook, under a framed portrait of the man he holds in highest <part>esteem</part>: himself. Same time, same towel, same smile. That's just his <kanji>usual</kanji>.
常.on: As usual, a <sound>jo</sound>ey pops out of the kangaroo's pouch next door and borrows the towel.
常.kun: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' Grandpa sneezes, as he does every morning, and a bird flies out of the <sound>ne</sound>st in his hair.

非.meaning: Two rows of short bars stand back to back on two tall spines, like a pair of doors slammed shut against each other. Knock, and both sides shout the same thing back at you: no, no, <kanji>not</kanji> today.
非.on: You try to wedge the doors open with a high <sound>hee</sound>l, but it snaps off: not a chance.
非.kun: Outside, a cheerleader chants '<sound>Ah</sound>! <sound>Rah</sound>!' at the doors, but the answer is still no.

待.meaning: At the foot of the mountain, a queue of monks stands in front of the <part>chairlift</part> up to the <part>temple</part>. It's stuck. They shuffle, they sigh, they count their prayer beads. All anyone can do is <kanji>wait</kanji>.
待.on: One bored monk knots his belt into a fancy <sound>tie</sound>, just to pass the time.
待.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>!' a little monk calls to his mum. 'Are we there yet?'

去.meaning: A gardener kneels on a mound of <part>soil</part>, his <part>elbow</part> deep in the hole where his prize carrot was. He digs, he gropes, and finds nothing but a tunnel. The carrot is <kanji>gone</kanji>.
去.on: Far down the tunnel, a mole is selling it at a little <sound>kio</sound>sk.
去.kun: The mole pays for a bus ticket with a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and leaves town for good.

丈.meaning: A tailor lays <part>one</part> long ribbon flat on the table and holds his open <part>scissors</part> over it, measuring twice before he cuts. Too short is no good, and too long is no better. He wants the exact <kanji>length</kanji>.
丈.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey leans out of its mum's pouch and holds the end of the tape for him.
丈.kun: '<sound>Ta</sound>-dah!' he cries, and measures a strand of <sound>ke</sound>lp against his own height.

他.meaning: You reach for your coat on the <part>coat hook</part>, but a <part>scorpion</part> is curled up in the sleeve, tail raised. You back away slowly. Never mind that one: you'll wear the <kanji>other</kanji> coat.
他.on: You fill a <sound>tu</sound>b with water and drop the scorpion's coat in, just to be sure.
他.kun: With a short '<sound>Ho</sound>!' you grab another coat, and the <sound>ca</sound>rp in the hall fish tank nods: good choice.

押.meaning: A knight in heavy <part>armor</part> leans his whole weight against a ship's <part>anchor</part> stuck in the beach. He groans, he strains, his metal boots slide in the sand, and inch by inch it moves. He gives one last <kanji>push</kanji>.
押.on: The anchor rolls down the beach and thuds into a huge <sound>oa</sound>k.
押.kun: A short '<sound>Oh</sound>!' and the knight shoves it the other way.

写.meaning: A child tucks a picture under a <part>blanket</part> of thin paper and traces every line with a crayon. Then she peels it off and goes to <part>bestow</part> it on her gran as her own work. It's a perfect <kanji>copy</kanji>.
写.on: Next she copies a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock, feather by feather.
写.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>!' says Gran, holding it up, and the crayon dust makes her sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

戦.meaning: Two kings start with a <part>simple</part> quarrel over a lantern. Then someone brings a <part>spear</part>, the other side brings two, and soon every field is full of shields and shouting. A small spat has become a <kanji>war</kanji>.
戦.on: A tired <sound>sen</sound>try stands at the castle gate, counting spears as they go past.
戦.kun: The armies run out of arrows and start throwing anything: an <sound>ee</sound>l, a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock, a <sound>sa</sound>rdine.

仲.meaning: Two neighbours won't speak, so they hang notes on a <part>coat hook</part> nailed to the fence, right in the <part>middle</part> between their gardens. Messages go back and forth all week. That hook is their <kanji>go-between</kanji>.
仲.on: One neighbour leaves a stick of <sound>chew</sound>ing gum on the hook as a peace offering.
仲.kun: The other leaves a warm <sound>na</sound>an and a <sound>ca</sound>rp, and now they get along fine.

選.meaning: Two <part>cobra</part> candidates sway on a stage while the crowd lifts it <part>together</part> and carries it up a <part>ramp</part> to the town hall. Whoever hisses best wins. The town is about to <kanji>elect</kanji> a snake.
選.on: The <sound>sen</sound>try at the town hall door checks every ballot for fang marks.
選.kun: The winning cobra chooses its prize: an <sound>e</sound>gg, and a '<sound>Rah</sound>!' from the crowd.

我.meaning: A soldier grabs a <part>spear</part> in one <part>hand</part>, points it at his own reflection and shouts, 'Look at me! Bravest, strongest, best!' Nobody else gets a word in. That's one huge <kanji>ego</kanji>.
我.on: He even carves his own name into a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic and wears it round his neck.
我.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' he gasps at his reflection. 'What a handsome <sound>re</sound>d face I have!'

怪.meaning: In a ghost town, a <part>tumbleweed</part> rolls up to your door, stops, and rolls back. Then it does it again. Your <part>heartbeat</part> thumps. Tumbleweeds don't knock. Something about this is very <kanji>suspicious</kanji>.
怪.on: Then a <sound>ki</sound>te with no string drifts down the empty street after it.
怪.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' you gasp: the tumbleweed trails a long red thread of <sound>ya</sound>rn, straight back to your own door.

連.meaning: You drive your <part>car</part> up the <part>ramp</part> onto the ferry, and behind it, tied on with rope, come your bike, your sofa and your grumpy cat in a cart. You never go anywhere alone: you <kanji>take along</kanji> everything.
連.on: A tiny <sound>wren</sound> hitches a ride on the roof rack too.
連.kun: The cat sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' and everything tied behind the car, all in one long line, answers '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

包.meaning: A <part>cobra</part> wants to give its friend a birthday present, but it has no hands. So it curls up on the paper itself, and the paper folds over its back in one big <part>wrap</part>. A gift that hisses: that's how snakes <kanji>wrap</kanji> things.
包.on: Its friend unwraps it with a blast from a garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
包.kun: Paper dust flies up its nose, and the cobra sneezes twice: '<sound>Tsu</sound>! <sound>Tsu</sound>!'

全.meaning: A tiny <part>king</part> stands under a giant <part>umbrella</part> in a storm. Not one drop touches him: not his crown, not his cape, not the tip of his toe. He stays dry, the <kanji>whole</kanji> of him.
全.on: Under the umbrella he rakes a little <sound>zen</sound> garden, perfectly calm.
全.kun: He bows to the soaked crowd with a hiccup stuck in the middle: '<sound>Ma</sound>… hic… <sound>ta</sound>-dah!' Completely dry.

器.meaning: Four <part>mouth</part>-shaped bowls sit at the corners of the table around a <part>large</part> cook, who spreads his arms and fills them all at once, a ladle in each hand: soup, rice, sauce, tea. Every bowl and ladle here is a <kanji>utensil</kanji>.
器.on: At night he locks them all in a cupboard with a big brass <sound>key</sound>.
器.kun: One bowl slips. '<sound>Oo</sound>!' gasps the cook, pepper flies, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' he sneezes, and '<sound>Wah</sound>!' he wails as it smashes.

機.meaning: A weaver cuts a <part>tree</part> into beams and pegs and asks the threads, '<part>How many</part> of you are there?' Thousands, they answer, and he strings up every one. Clack, clack: his wooden frame is a <kanji>loom</kanji>.
機.on: Every morning he winds it up with a big brass <sound>key</sound>, like a clock.
機.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laughs the weaver as the loom clatters out a scarf, a sock and a <sound>ta</sound>co-shaped hat.

飛.meaning: Two pairs of wings sweep out to the right of a tall body, each tipped with tiny feathers, one pair above the other. They flap, the body lifts, and up it goes over the rooftops. It can <kanji>fly</kanji>.
飛.on: In its beak it carries a red high <sound>hee</sound>l, stolen from a balcony.
飛.kun: It lands on top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole to rest its wings.

商.meaning: A trader climbs up to <part>stand</part> on a wooden <part>frame</part> stall, <part>legs</part> planted wide, and his big <part>mouth</part> never stops: 'Apples! Pots! Socks! Two for one!' Coins clink into his apron all day. He is <kanji>selling</kanji>.
商.on: At noon he puts on a <sound>show</sound>, juggling his apples to pull in the crowd.
商.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' he shouts, waving a brass <sound>key</sound> in one hand and a warm <sound>na</sound>an in the other. 'Buy now!'
